text: I am a stonecutter and recently I have been having problems lifting heavier stones. In a week we need to gather enough stone for the construction of a new monastery in the town. The work is so much, I need to pack 10 oxen with stone, but I can barely pack 8. Please help me.

Since the spring floods a fever has come over me every night, and by day I am so slow and heavy-limbed that I stumble on the path and spill the water I carry up from the well. Old Marta told me of the pond where the river bends below the mill: the plants on its banks cleanse anything, she said, and no fever outlasts a brew of them. So I picked a basketful, steeped it in ale and drank, and she spoke true: that night the fever did not come. But every cup leaves me dizzy, the room turns about me, and before long I am retching in the yard. If I leave the ale for a day, the fever returns and the slowness with it. I can neither keep drinking it nor stop. Please, help me.
